beats.text: Why do GPUs sit idle during LLM inference until The Death of One-Hot Vectors unlocks 7x throughput?
beats.visual_focus: A massive, sparse 50k-dimensional coordinate grid with dots at right angles.

beats.text: The villain is the memory wall; storing millions of discrete dimensions wastes massive compute on mostly empty, sparse index matrices.
beats.visual_focus: A memory buffer being flooded with zeroes, wasting bandwidth for a single active bit.

beats.text: We collapse this dimension, projecting words into a dense, continuous latent space where semantic similarity defines geometric proximity.
beats.visual_focus: A dense vector cloud morphing from a grid into a cohesive geometric manifold.

Standard transformer architectures hit an invisible memory wall that The Death of One-Hot Vectors finally breaks.
Why is The Death of One-Hot Vectors a major breakthrough? Because we propose two novel model architectures for computing continuous vector representations of words from very large data sets.
